text:
morgan: Heads-up — we have a pretty large ML checkpointing job hitting prod de-staging next Wed, 02:00 UTC. It will snapshot ~18TB across ~40 nodes over a 2h window. I expect bursty snapshot API calls and sustained EBS gp3 IOPS. Can we raise snapshot throttle and EBS IOPS limits in us-west-2 for acct 012345678901?

cloud-ops: Thanks — can you paste the rough IOPS and snapshot/sec numbers you expect? also attach the account and region (you already did acct) and whether these are gp3/io2.

morgan: Plan is gp3 volumes (baseline 3000 IOPS currently), we’ll stripe 2 volumes per node for throughput. Peak write IOPS ~= 200k across the fleet, snapshot create rate ~3-4/s (many parallel snapshots triggered by the app). Snapshot total size ~18TB, but many deltas.

laura: That snapshot create rate will definitely hit the API throttle if we do them serially. Could we queue snapshot jobs and pace them? Or use incremental chained snapshots to reduce parallel calls?

ben: Cost note: increasing IOPS and switching to io2 will bump costs a lot; we should compare to using S3 multi-part upload of checkpoints as a temporary fallback.

arjun: Another mitigation: spin up a temporary staging bucket in GCS in us-west1 and upload checkpoint shards from nodes, then import. That avoids snapshot API pressure but adds egress/transfer cost and code change.

cloud-ops: OK — will open a provider quota request. For AWS we need exact quotas: EBS IOPS per region (requested 300k) and EBS Snapshot API rate limit increase to at least 10/s for the account. Also request ENI attach limits? not necessary for this but confirm instance type. Any instance lifecycle churn?

morgan: Instances are p4d and g5 clusters, no mass reboots planned during snapshot window. We only need the IOPS and snapshot rate increases. Requesting: EBS gp3 IOPS soft limit -> 300k IOPS (us-west-2), Snapshot API throttle -> 10 req/s, Concurrent snapshots -> 100. Account 012345678901.

cloud-ops: Copying the exact payload I used in the support case below, so you all have a record:```
Service: Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS)
Limit: gp3 Provisioned IOPS (regional)
Current: 50000
Requested: 300000
Region: us-west-2
Rationale: Scheduled ML checkpointing workload will create parallel snapshots and perform sustained gp3 writes across ~40 nodes for 2 hours on 2026-03-25 02:00 UTC. Failure to increase will cause snapshot throttling and prolong job completion, impacting customer SLAs.
---
Service: Amazon EC2 API (EBS Snapshot requests)
Limit: Snapshot creation API rate
Current: 5 req/s
Requested: 10 req/s
Region: us-west-2
Rationale: Concurrent snapshot creates by distributed checkpointing system.
```

sre-bot: [incident] created support case AWS-1234567890 for EBS quota increase (submitted by cloud-ops). Estimated response: 48-72h.

laura: If AWS turnaround is >48h we should run the paced snapshot fallback. Morgan can you add a feature flag to throttle snapshot starts to 2/s?

morgan: Yep I’ll add a flag today and a circuit to switch to S3 upload if snapshots start failing.

cloud-ops: AWS case filed: Case ID AWS-1234567890. ETA 2-3 days. I also asked for a temporary soft increase while they review. If approved we’ll postback here and tag infra-announce.

ben: Please also include a note to billing that this might spike IOPS costs for the snapshot window. I’ll estimate delta and post in the billing channel.

arjun: One more note — if we end up striping volumes, ensure we pre-warm with fio or set throughput settings before the run. Cold GP3 may have initial limits.

morgan: Good call. I’ll run a pre-warm job tonight against a small subset, and will post results. Thanks all :thumbsup:

cloud-ops: Logging action items: 1) monitoring: add Alert on Snapshot API 429s (arjun), 2) throttle flag in app (morgan), 3) AWS quota case (cloud-ops case AWS-1234567890), 4) pre-warm plan (morgan). Closing thread when quota confirmed.
